clue.text: Smorgasbord in Polish and in French

parts.note: to polish is to buff, as in buffing a shoe
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A Swedish spread being described in two other languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the verb, capitalised only because it starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a self-service spread of many dishes, just like a Scandinavian smorgasbord.

clue.text: America, say, brought up tradition

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated EG (exempli gratia)

explanation.surface: A national custom one was raised with in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America, say' reads as one example of a country, but 'say' is its own piece; 'brought up' reverses only that piece, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or practice, which is what a tradition is.

clue.text: Criminal fake fur trades

indicators.note: fake suggests something made up or reworked, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook selling counterfeit fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' looks like an adjective for the fur but signals rearranging FUR TRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudster is a cheat or swindler, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Revolutionary chat after extra time and one could end up in hot water

definitions.text: one could end up in hot water

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to gab is to chat
AET is the football scoreline abbreviation for a result after extra time

explanation.surface: Radical talk following a long football match, and someone gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses GABAET as a whole. 'In hot water' looks like trouble but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag is literally dropped into a cup of hot water to brew.

clue.text: Oblique art about poetry

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word art is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Indirect, slanted art concerning poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but reverses ART to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, traverse means lying across or transverse, so running at a slant.

clue.text: Dawn — possibly after escort will suspiciously disappear

indicators.note: after places the comedian's surname following the escort word

parts.note: to take someone somewhere is to escort them
Dawn French is a British comedian, so Dawn is a possible first name for French
to will something is to leave it to someone in a will

explanation.surface: Someone called Dawn, accompanied, will vanish under a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a well-known British comic actress. The phrase means to slip away without permission or notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To take French leave is an idiom for leaving abruptly without asking permission or saying goodbye.

clue.text: Cancelled edition after warning us regularly — all except the leader

indicators.note: after puts the edition abbreviation at the end
regularly means every other letter of the next words is taken
the leader is the first letter, which is dropped from the word all

explanation.surface: A publisher pulled an issue after a warning was issued to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'warning us'; 'except the leader' drops the first letter of 'all'; 'after' puts the edition abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul something is to declare it void, the same as cancelling it.

clue.text: Commend European vote to Lords, initially

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of Lords is used

explanation.surface: Praising a European vote being passed to the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes L from Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is to commend.

clue.text: Sub-post office rejected sensible legal documents

parts.note: SUB and PO, abbreviations for sub- and post office

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for sensible is read in reverse

parts.note: sane means sensible

explanation.surface: A small post office turning away sensible legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SANE into ENAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Subpoenas are writs ordering a person to attend court, so they are legal documents.

clue.text: Embargo article when family reveals potential hazard

parts.note: an embargo is a ban
an is the indefinite article
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
kin means family

explanation.surface: A family reveals a ban on an item, exposing a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a slipping danger, literally or figuratively a pitfall.

clue.text: Held in the button — turned over TV

indicators.note: turned over means the concealed letters are read backwards
held in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pressing the button and switching on the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in' picks BUT from 'the button' together with the E; 'turned over' reads tHE BUTton backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The tube is informal slang for the television, from the old cathode-ray picture tube.

clue.text: Sitcom star

explanation.surface: A television comedy celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the BBC space comedy is also an astronomical term for a small dim star.

clue.text: Bound to apply 1p discount to sticky sweet

indicators.note: discount means taking something off, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: a lollipop is a sticky sweet on a stick
1p read as the letters I and P

explanation.surface: Obliged to take a penny off a lolly.
explanation.walkthrough: '1p' is read as IP, removed from LOLLIPOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move with ungainly bounds, so it is a verb for bounding.

clue.text: Every now and then Aztecs ate relish

indicators.note: every now and then means taking alternate letters from the next words

explanation.surface: The Aztecs occasionally ate a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every now and then' picks the even letters of aZtEcS aTe.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto or keen enjoyment, the same sense as relish.

clue.text: Memphis rocked after Elvis's first high-class number one, say

indicators.note: after places the rearranged city behind the first two letters
first takes only the opening letter of Elvis's

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class, high-class

indicators.note: rocked means shaken up, so the letters of Memphis are rearranged

explanation.surface: Memphis rocked after Elvis's first classy chart-topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocked' rearranges MEMPHIS into PHEMISM. 'Number one' looks like a chart-topper.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Number one' is a polite way of saying urination, so it is an example of a euphemism.

clue.text: Simple and effective coat of polish for grand trunk — and its owner?

indicators.note: for means one thing replaces another here

parts.note: elegant can mean neatly simple and effective, as an elegant solution
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: a coat is the outside, so the outer letters of polish are taken

explanation.surface: A simple way to polish a grand old travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat of polish' gives PH, which replaces G in ELEGANT. The trunk looks like luggage but is a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is an elephant's nose, so the animal is the owner of the trunk.

clue.text: Hotel prepared real, protein-rich seeds but not on account of this clown

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: prepared means reworked, so the letters of real are rearranged
but not means the following abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: quinoa is a protein-rich seed
OA is the abbreviation for on account

explanation.surface: A hotel serves real quinoa, but a clown objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' turns REAL into ARLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the classic clown or buffoon of the commedia dell'arte and pantomime.

clue.text: Diagnose current depression — condition society ultimately supports

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letter sits beneath the rest

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a dent is a depression
if introduces a condition

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of society

explanation.surface: A doctor spots depression, a condition society ultimately helps with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current depression' reads as mood; it is two pieces. 'supports' puts Y at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify an illness, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Occasional content for radio inspired by rotating crops

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the radio letters go inside the crops word
rotating means turned round, so crops is read backwards
content means what is inside, so the middle letters of radio are taken

explanation.surface: Occasional radio material drawn from crop rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' makes SPORC; ADI from rADIo goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means happening at irregular intervals, which is occasional.

clue.text: Half of Mark's gamble

indicators.note: half of means the word is cut, keeping only its second half

parts.note: an asterisk is a mark used in printing

explanation.surface: Mark is betting half his money.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is a printed mark, ASTERISK, whose back half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to stake it on an uncertain outcome, which is to gamble.

clue.text: Absorb some of Rob's essay …

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting engrossed in part of a student's essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to preoccupy someone completely, as an absorbing interest does.

clue.text: Ground supplied by river heading away from spring, perhaps

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: spring is an example of a season

explanation.surface: Land supplied by a river flowing from its source.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like a water source; it is a season, which loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground is a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint.

clue.text: … Rob's essay reportedly covering the disheartened Left

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around the following letters
reportedly means as heard, so a word is replaced by letters of the same sound

parts.note: essay said aloud sounds like the two letters S and A

indicators.note: without its heart, only the outer letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Rob's essay apparently covers depressed left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue. 'reportedly' turns 'essay' into the letters it sounds like; 'disheartened' drops the middle of 'the'; 'covering' wraps one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to steal, the two verbs being synonyms.

clue.text: Retiring Hammy Hamster-like creature after the first book

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so all the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: hammy acting is over the top, OTT

indicators.note: after the first means only what follows the first letter is used

parts.note: a gerbil is a small rodent like a hamster

explanation.surface: A shy children's TV hamster after the first edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammy Hamster was a children's TV rodent, but here it splits. ERBIL joins OTT and 'Retiring' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the book, the text, of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Make for Italy, that's suffering coastal erosion

parts.note: for can mean to, as in the key for the door

indicators.note: losing its coast means the outer letters of Italy wear away

explanation.surface: Heading for Italy, whose coastline is being eroded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering coastal erosion' takes the ends off ITALY to leave TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To total is to add up to, as in two and two make four.

clue.text: Dance most of jig in front of empty venue

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second
most of means the last letter is dropped
empty means the inside is removed, so only the outer letters of venue remain

explanation.surface: A jig danced in front of an empty hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively swing dance style.

clue.text: Making equine data jockey will be wanting

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Racing form for horses that falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like a rider beside 'equine' but signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting means lacking or not good enough, so it is the same as inadequate.

clue.text: Worker in timeless place of worship penning detailed proclamation

indicators.note: penning means enclosing the following letters
timeless means without time, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship

indicators.note: detailed means losing the tail, its last letter

parts.note: oyez is the town crier's call before a proclamation

explanation.surface: A worker in an ageless temple writing out a long announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' turns TEMPLE into EMPLE; 'detailed' cuts OYEZ to OYE.
explanation.definitionFit: An employee is someone hired to work, a worker.

clue.text: One small fireplace

parts.note: an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: One little hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one only, a lone item.
